summary.en: Youth protests are challenging Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Delhi while small protests continue, and a man attempted to force his way into the Chhattisgarh chief minister's house, leading to clashes with police. An explosion near the Line of Control in Poonch raised casualty fears, and a landmine blast killed four near the LoC in Kashmir; a teenager also died after his vehicle plunged off a road in Rajouri. In Manipur, the Border Security Force director general reviewed security and operational preparedness amid fresh violence, and the state chief minister met BJP legislators to discuss security and development priorities. The DGP in Kashmir reviewed security and called for intensified intelligence-based operations, while juveniles fled a safety home in Chhattisgarh. The conflict has resulted in 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Ungdomsprotester utfordrer statsminister Narendra Modi i Delhi mens små protester fortsetter, og en mann forsøkte å bryte seg inn i huset til sjefministeren i Chhattisgarh, noe som førte til sammenstøt med politiet. En eksplosjon nær grensen mot Pakistan i Poonch vekket frykt for tap, og en landmineeksplosjon drepte fire nær grensen i Kashmir; en tenåring døde også etter at kjøretøyet hans falt ned fra en vei i Rajouri. I Manipur gjennomgikk Border Security Force-direktøren sikkerhet og operasjonell beredskap etter ny vold, og delstatens sjefminister møtte BJP-lovgivere for å diskutere sikkerhets- og utviklingsprioriteringer. DGP i Kashmir gjennomgikk sikkerheten og oppfordret til intensivering av etterretningsbaserte operasjoner, mens mindreårige flyktet fra et sikkerhetshjem i Chhattisgarh. Konflikten har resultert i 437 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
